note: Provisional statements written from reading the table; the maintainer replaces them.

statements.text: cnt depends on the hour of the day (hr)
temp and atemp are nearly collinear
instant is a row number and dteday the time axis
rentals concentrate in rush hours on working days: 35.9% of all rentals sit on 17.2% of rows (2.09x their row share)
statements.note: Measured: the cell workingday = 1 and hr in (7, 8, 9, 17, 18, 19) holds 2,983 of 17,379 rows (17.2%) and 1,181,285 of 3,292,679 rentals (35.9%), 2.09x its row share. The concentration is measure-weighted: it lives in the cnt values over the cell, not in the cell's row count (row counts over the (workingday, hr) grid track independence almost exactly). In the unhinted runs no pass states it: the hotspots pass counts rows, and this concentration lives in the cnt values. With cnt declared through the weights hint, the weighted scan states the cell (issue #329); the gate's weighted component scores this statement as must-tier in that hinted run, and its miss in the unhinted runs is the measurement.

statements.text: Statements that restate the calendar: every column is dteday or a column dteday determines (yr, mnth, season, weekday, holiday, workingday)
statements.note: Each of yr, mnth, season, weekday, holiday and workingday takes one value per dteday. A level shift in yr, a spike in holiday, a hotspot of weekday x workingday, or season predicted from mnth states the calendar, not the data. A single-column concentration (holiday is 97% 0) and an incomplete period are facts about the data and are not counted.

statements.text: hr or instant treated as an entity followed through time
statements.note: hr is the hour of the day (0-23, crossed with every date) and instant is the row number; neither is an entity that enters, exits, or accumulates a total.
